name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q01 - Matching taxonomical aids with their functions

questiontext.text:
Match the taxonomical aids with their correct descriptions and choose the correct option.

Column I Column II
A. Herbarium i. Specialised gardens having collections of living plants for reference
B. Botanical Gardens ii. Places where wild animals are kept in protected environments under human care
C. Museum iii. Store house of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed, and preserved on sheets
D. Zoological Parks iv. Collections of preserved plant and animal specimens in jars or as dry specimens

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Taxonomical aids are procedures and techniques used by biologists to store and preserve specimens as well as information for identification and classification of organisms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Taxonomical Aid
A herbarium is a store house of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed, and preserved on sheets arranged according to a universally accepted system of classification. Botanical gardens are specialised gardens that maintain collections of living plants for reference and identification, with each plant labelled with its botanical name and family. Biological museums are generally set up in educational institutes and hold collections of preserved plant and animal specimens in preservative solutions, as dry specimens, pinned insects, or stuffed larger animals. Zoological parks (zoos) are places where wild animals are kept in protected environments under human care to study their food habits and behaviour.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Herbarium corresponds to the store house of dried, pressed, and preserved plant specimens on sheets; Botanical Gardens correspond to specialised gardens with living plants for reference; Museum corresponds to collections of preserved plant and animal specimens in jars or as dry specimens; and Zoological Parks correspond to places where wild animals are kept in protected environments under human care. Thus, the correct pairing is A-iii, B-i, C-iv, D-ii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q02 - Matching organisms with modes of reproduction and growth

questiontext.text:
Match the organisms with their characteristic mode of reproduction or growth and choose the correct option.

Column I Column II
A. Planaria i. Fragmentation
B. Yeast and Hydra ii. Growth synonymous with reproduction
C. Protonema of mosses iii. True regeneration
D. Amoeba iv. Budding

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Living organisms exhibit diverse modes of asexual reproduction and growth depending on their cellular organisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Organism
Planaria (flat worms) exhibit true regeneration, where a fragmented organism regenerates the lost part of its body and becomes a new organism. Lower organisms such as yeast and Hydra reproduce asexually by budding. Fungi, filamentous algae, and the protonema of mosses multiply easily by fragmentation. In unicellular organisms like bacteria, unicellular algae, and Amoeba, reproduction is synonymous with growth, meaning an increase in the number of cells.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Planaria matches with true regeneration, yeast and Hydra match with budding, protonema of mosses matches with fragmentation, and Amoeba matches with growth synonymous with reproduction. Thus, the correct pairing is A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q03 - Matching organisms with their family and order

questiontext.text:
Match the organisms with their respective Family and Order and choose the correct option.

Column I Column II
A. Man (Homo sapiens) i. Family: Anacardiaceae; Order: Sapindales
B. Housefly (Musca domestica) ii. Family: Poaceae; Order: Poales
C. Mango (Mangifera indica) iii. Family: Hominidae; Order: Primata
D. Wheat (Triticum aestivum) iv. Family: Muscidae; Order: Diptera

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Every known organism is placed in a taxonomic hierarchy consisting of species, genus, family, order, class, phylum or division, and kingdom.

Step 2: Evaluation of Taxonomic Categories
Man (Homo sapiens) belongs to the genus Homo, family Hominidae, order Primata, class Mammalia, and phylum Chordata. Housefly (Musca domestica) belongs to the genus Musca, family Muscidae, order Diptera, class Insecta, and phylum Arthropoda. Mango (Mangifera indica) belongs to the genus Mangifera, family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, class Dicotyledonae, and division Angiospermae. Wheat (Triticum aestivum) belongs to the genus Triticum, family Poaceae, order Poales, class Monocotyledonae, and division Angiospermae.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Man matches with Family Hominidae and Order Primata; Housefly matches with Family Muscidae and Order Diptera; Mango matches with Family Anacardiaceae and Order Sapindales; and Wheat matches with Family Poaceae and Order Poales. Thus, the correct pairing is A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q04 - Matching related genera and families to higher taxa

questiontext.text:
Match the groups of genera or families with the taxonomic category in which they are placed and choose the correct option.

Column I Column II
A. Solanum, Petunia, and Datura i. Order Carnivora
B. Panthera and Felis ii. Order Polymoniales
C. Felidae and Canidae iii. Family Solanaceae
D. Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae iv. Family Felidae

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A family comprises a group of related genera with fewer similarities compared to genus and species, whereas an order is an assemblage of families exhibiting a few similar characters.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Group
Among plants, the three different genera Solanum, Petunia, and Datura are placed together in the family Solanaceae based on vegetative and reproductive features. Among animals, the genus Panthera (lion, tiger, leopard) is placed along with the genus Felis (cats) in the family Felidae. The animal families Felidae (cats) and Canidae (dogs) are included in the order Carnivora. Plant families such as Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on floral characters.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Solanum, Petunia, and Datura belong to Family Solanaceae; Panthera and Felis belong to Family Felidae; Felidae and Canidae belong to Order Carnivora; and Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae belong to Order Polymoniales. Thus, the correct pairing is A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q05 - Matching taxonomic literature and keys with descriptions

questiontext.text:
Match the taxonomical aids used for recording descriptions and identification with their correct meanings and choose the correct option.

Column I Column II
A. Key i. Contains information on any one taxon
B. Flora ii. Provides information for identification of names of species found in an area
C. Manuals iii. Analytical aid based on contrasting characters generally in a pair called couplet
D. Monographs iv. Contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Taxonomists use specialised keys and published records such as flora, manuals, and monographs to facilitate correct identification of organisms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Aid
A taxonomic key is an analytical aid used for the identification of plants and animals based on similarities and dissimilarities, relying on contrasting characters generally in a pair called a couplet, where each statement is called a lead. Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area and provides an index to the plant species found there. Manuals are useful in providing information for the identification of names of species found in an area. Monographs contain comprehensive information on any one taxon.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Key matches with the analytical aid based on contrasting characters in a couplet; Flora matches with the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area; Manuals match with information for identification of names of species found in an area; and Monographs match with information on any one taxon. Thus, the correct pairing is A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q06 - Matching characteristics of living organisms with defining status

questiontext.text:
Match the features of living organisms with their correct status and justification, then choose the correct option.

Column I Column II
A. Growth i. Defining feature without exception; isolated in vitro reactions are living reactions, not living things
B. Reproduction ii. Defining property involving awareness of surroundings and response to environmental stimuli
C. Metabolism iii. Non-defining feature because non-living objects can also increase in mass by surface accumulation
D. Consciousness iv. Non-defining feature because sterile organisms like mules and worker bees do not exhibit it

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A defining property of living organisms must be exhibited universally by all living organisms without exception and must be absent in non-living objects.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Feature
Growth is not a defining property because if increase in body mass is taken as a criterion, non-living objects like mountains, boulders, and sand mounds also grow by accumulation of material on the surface, whereas in living organisms growth is from inside. Reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic because many living organisms such as mules, sterile worker bees, and infertile human couples do not reproduce. Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception and no non-living object exhibits it; isolated metabolic reactions performed in vitro in cell-free systems are neither living nor non-living things, though they are living reactions. Consciousness—the ability to sense the environment and respond to physical, chemical, or biological stimuli—is exhibited by all organisms from prokaryotes to eukaryotes and is a defining property of living organisms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Growth matches with being a non-defining feature because non-living objects can increase in mass by surface accumulation; Reproduction matches with being a non-defining feature because sterile organisms do not exhibit it; Metabolism matches with being a defining feature without exception where isolated in vitro reactions are living reactions; and Consciousness matches with being a defining property involving awareness and response to environmental stimuli. Thus, the correct pairing is A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q07 - Matching taxonomic concepts, codes, and scientists

questiontext.text:
Match the concepts, codes, and scientist with their correct descriptions and choose the correct option.

Column I Column II
A. Binomial nomenclature i. Study of diversity of organisms and their evolutionary relationships; derived from Latin word systema
B. ICBN ii. Pioneered the currently accepted definition of a biological species and awarded the triple crown of biology
C. Systematics iii. Two-component naming system using generic name and specific epithet given by Carolus Linnaeus
D. Ernst Mayr iv. Provides agreed principles and criteria for assigning scientific names to plants

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Standardised scientific naming and classification systems allow biologists worldwide to identify organisms unambiguously and understand their evolutionary relationships.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Entry
Binomial nomenclature is the system of providing a scientific name with two components—the generic name and the specific epithet—and was given by Carolus Linnaeus. The International Code for Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN) provides the agreed principles and criteria on which scientific names for plants are based (whereas ICZN is for animals). Systematics, derived from the Latin word systema meaning systematic arrangement of organisms, takes into account evolutionary relationships between organisms in addition to identification, nomenclature, and classification. Ernst Mayr, called 'The Darwin of the 20th century', pioneered the currently accepted definition of a biological species and was awarded the triple crown of biology (Balzan Prize, International Prize for Biology, and Crafoord Prize).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Binomial nomenclature matches with the two-component naming system given by Carolus Linnaeus; ICBN matches with agreed principles and criteria for assigning scientific names to plants; Systematics matches with the study of diversity and evolutionary relationships derived from systema; and Ernst Mayr matches with pioneering the biological species definition and winning the triple crown of biology. Thus, the correct pairing is A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii.
